what_it_is.prose: BrahMos Aerospace Private Limited (BAPL) is an India-Russia joint venture formed in 1998 by DRDO (India, 50.5%) and NPO Mashinostroyenia (NPOM, Russia, 49.5%) with an authorised capital of USD 300 million. Headquartered at 16 Cariappa Marg, Kirby Place, New Delhi, BrahMos Aerospace manufactures the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile — named after the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers — across land, ship, air, and submarine-launched variants. The basic BrahMos has a 290 km range and flies at Mach 2.8-3, derived from the Russian P-800 Oniks/Yakhont. The Extended Range (ER) variant, enabled by India's accession to the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR) in 2016, achieves 800 km range and is in multi-phase trials through 2026 with induction expected within 2-3 years per Defence.in. The BrahMos-NG (Next Generation) is a smaller, lighter variant targeting 290-450 km range but has reportedly been delayed in 2025-26. The BrahMos-II hypersonic variant (Mach 7-8, 1,500 km range) was reportedly paused in May 2026 per The Eurasian Times, though BrahMos.com still lists it as a 'conceptualised hypersonic weapon of the future'. BAPL is not a separately listed entity and does not publish an annual report URL; revenue and order book are not publicly disclosed. Major disclosed contracts include a ₹4,000+ crore land-based BrahMos-ER order for the Indian Army in April 2024 (for 2 regiments with 800 km range), a ₹1,700 crore Indian Navy order for ship-launched BrahMos in 2023, and a ₹2,500 crore air-launched BrahMos upgrade in 2024. BrahMos has achieved major export success: Philippines signed a $375 million contract on 28 January 2022 for the Shore-Based Anti-Ship Missile System (deliveries 2024-25, 3 batteries complete); Indonesia reached agreement in July 2026 for ~$450 million (with Astra BVRAAM package); Vietnam is reportedly near finalisation. Cumulative BrahMos orders across all variants and customers are estimated at >₹30,000 crore.

deployments_procurement.summary: BrahMos is in operational service across all three Indian services — Indian Army (land-launched regiments), Indian Navy (ship and submarine launched), and IAF (air-launched from Su-30MKI). Cumulative Indian orders are estimated at >₹30,000 crore. Major disclosed contracts include ₹4,000+ crore BrahMos-ER land order (April 2024, 2 regiments), ₹1,700 crore Navy ship-launched (2023), and ₹2,500 crore air-launched upgrade (2024). Export success includes Philippines $375M (January 2022, deliveries 2024-25), Indonesia ~$450M (July 2026), and Vietnam reportedly near finalisation.

faq.question: Who owns BrahMos Aerospace?
faq.answer: BrahMos Aerospace Private Limited (BAPL) is a 50.5% / 49.5% joint venture between India's Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyenia (NPOM), formed in 1998 with an authorised capital of USD 300 million. The JV is named after the Brahmaputra (India) and Moskva (Russia) rivers. DRDO provides the inertial navigation, mission software, and mobile launchers; NPOM provides the airframe, propulsion (ramjet based on the P-800 Oniks/Yakhont), and seeker lineage.

faq.question: What is the BrahMos-ER 800 km variant?
faq.answer: The BrahMos-ER (Extended Range) achieves 800 km range, enabled by India's accession to the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR) in 2016 which removed the 300 km range cap on Indian exports. The Indian Army placed a ₹4,000+ crore order in April 2024 for two BrahMos-ER regiments. After a successful 2025 test, the BrahMos-LR (Long Range) entered a multi-phase trial schedule for 2026 with induction expected within 2-3 years per Defence.in.

faq.question: Has BrahMos been exported?
faq.answer: Yes. The Philippines signed a $375 million contract on 28 January 2022 for the Shore-Based Anti-Ship Missile System — the first export of an Indian strategic missile. Deliveries began in April 2024 and 3 batteries have been delivered. Indonesia reached agreement in July 2026 for approximately $450 million (with an Astra BVRAAM package). Vietnam is reportedly near finalisation. Reuters reported in October 2022 that BAPL hoped for $5 billion in cumulative supersonic missile exports by 2025.
